name: AffineRatio
description: Returns the affine ratio λ of three collinear points A , B and C , where C = A + λ * AB .

name: Angle
description: Conic: Returns the angle of twist of a conic section’s major axis (see command Axes ).
syntax: Angle(y = x + 2, y = 2x + 3) yields 18.43° or the corresponding value in radians .
Angle(Line((-2, 0, 0), (0, 0, 2)), Line((2, 0, 0), (0, 0, 2))) yields 90° or the corresponding value in radians .
Angle(Line((1, 2, 3),(-2, -2, 0)), z = 0) yields 30.96° or the corresponding value in radians .
Angle(2x - y + z = 0, z = 0) yields 114.09° or the corresponding value in radians .

name: AngleBisector
description: Returns both angle bisectors of the lines.

name: Arc
description: Returns the directed arc (counterclockwise) of the given circle, with endpoints M and N.

name: Area
description: Calculates the area of the polygon defined by the given points.

name: AreCollinear
description: Decides if the points are collinear.

name: AreConcurrent
description:
Decides if the lines are concurrent. If the lines are parallel, they considered to have a common point in infinity,
thus this command returns true in this case.

name: AreConcyclic
description: Decides if the points are concyclic.

name: AreCongruent
description: Decides if the objects are congruent.

name: AreEqual
description: Decides if the objects are equal.
syntax: AreEqual(Segment((1, 2), (3, 4)), Segment((3, 4), (1, 6))) is different from Segment((1, 2), (3, 4)) == Segment((3, 4), (1, 6)) as the latter compares just the lengths

name: AreParallel
description: Decides if the lines are parallel.

name: ArePerpendicular
description:
Decides if the lines are perpendicular.
Normally this command computes the result numerically. This behavior can be changed by using the Prove command.

name: Barycenter
description: This command differs among variants of English:
syntax:
Barycenter({(2, 0), (0, 2), (-2, 0), (0, -2)}, {2, 1, 1, 1}) yields point B(0.4, 0) . The x -coordinate of
this point was determined by \( \frac{1}{ 2+1+1+1 }*(2*2+1*0+1*(-2)+1*0)\) = \(\frac{1}{ 5 }*2\) = 0.4

name: Centroid
description: Returns the centroid of the polygon.

name: Circle
description: Yields a circle with given center and radius.

name: CircularArc
description: Creates a circular arc with midpoint between the two points.

name: CircularSector
description: Creates a circular sector with midpoint between the two points.

name: CircumcircularArc
description:
Creates a circular arc through three points, where the first point is the starting point and the third point is the
endpoint of the circumcircular arc.

name: CircumcircularSector
description:
Creates a circular sector whose arc runs through the three points, where the first point is the starting point and the
third point is the endpoint of the arc.

name: Circumference
description: If the given conic is a circle or ellipse, this command returns its circumference. Otherwise the result is undefined.

name: ClosestPoint
description: Returns a new point on a path which is the closest to a selected point.

name: ClosestPointRegion
description: Returns a new point on the region which is the closest to a selected point.

name: CrossRatio
description: Calculates the cross ratio λ of four collinear points A , B , C and D , where: λ = AffineRatio[B, C, D ] / AffineRatio[A, C, D ].

name: Cubic
description: Gives n -th triangle cubic of the given triangle ABC .

name: Difference
description: Finds the difference of the two polygons.

name: Direction
description: Yields the direction vector of the line.

name: Distance
description: Yields the shortest distance between a point and an object.

name: Envelope
description:
Creates the envelope equation of a set of output paths while the
moving point is bound to another object.

name: Incircle
description:
Returns Incircle of the triangle formed by the
three Points.

name: InteriorAngles
description: Creates all the interior angles of the given polygon.

name: Intersect
description: Yields the intersection points of two objects.
syntax: Intersect(y = x + 3, Curve(t, 2t, t, 0, 10)) yields A =(3, 6).
Intersect(Curve(2s, 5s, s,-10, 10), Curve(t, 2t, t, -10, 10)) yields A =(0, 0).

Intersect( <Line> , <Object> ) creates the intersection point(s) of a line and a plane, segment, polygon, conic,
etc.
Intersect( <Plane> , <Object> ) creates the intersection point(s) of a plane and segment, polygon, conic, etc.
Intersect( <Conic>, <Conic> ) creates the intersection point(s) of two conics
Intersect( <Plane>, <Plane> ) creates the intersection line of two planes
Intersect( <Plane>, <Polyhedron> ) creates the polygon(s) intersection of a plane and a polyhedron.
Intersect( <Sphere>, <Sphere> ) creates the circle intersection of two spheres

Intersect( <Plane>, <Quadric> ) creates the conic intersection of the plane and the quadric (sphere, cone,
cylinder, …​)

name: IntersectPath
description: Creates the intersection path between line and polygon.

name: IsInRegion
description: Returns true if the point is in given region and false otherwise.

name: IsTangent
description: Decides if the line is tangent to the conic.

name: Length
description: Yields the length of the object.
syntax: Length( <Vector> ) yields the length of the vector.
Length( <Point> ) yields the length of the position vector of the given point.
Length( <List> ) yields the length of the list, which is the number of elements in the list.
Length( <Text> ) yields the number of characters in the text.
Length( <Locus> ) returns the number of points that the given locus is made up of. Use Perimeter (Locus) to get the length of the locus itself. For details see the article about First Command .
Length( <Arc> ) returns the arc length (i.e. just the length of the curved section) of an arc or sector.

name: Line
description: Creates a line through two points A and B .

name: Locus
description: Returns the locus curve of the point Q , which depends on the point P .
syntax: Locus( <Point Creating Locus Line Q>, <Point P>)
Locus( <Point Creating Locus Line Q>, <Slider t>)

name: LocusEquation
description: Calculates the equation of a Locus and plots this as an Implicit Curve.
syntax: LocusEquation( <Point Creating Locus Line Q>, <Point P> )

name: Midpoint
description: Returns the midpoint of the segment.

name: PathParameter
description: Returns the parameter (i.e. a number ranging from 0 to 1 ) of the point that belongs to a path .

name: Perimeter
description: Returns the perimeter of the polygon.

name: PerpendicularBisector
description: Yields the perpendicular bisector of a segment.

name: PerpendicularLine
description: Creates a line through the point perpendicular to the given line.
syntax:
PerpendicularLine( <Point>, <Line>, <Plane> ) creates a perpendicular line to the given line through the point and
parallel to the plane.

PerpendicularLine( <Point>, <Line>, space ) creates a perpendicular line to the given line through the point. The
two lines have an intersection point. This command yields undefined if the point is on the line in 3D.

name: Point
description: Returns a point on the geometric object. The resulting point can be moved along the path .

name: PointIn
description: Returns a point restricted to given region .

name: Polygon
description: Returns a polygon defined by the given points.

name: Polyline
description:
Creates an open polygonal chain (i.e. a connected series of segments) having the initial vertex in the first point of
the list, and the final vertex in the last point of the list.

name: Prove
description: Returns whether the given boolean expression is true or false in general.

name: ProveDetails
description: Returns some details of the result of the automated proof.

name: Radius
description: Returns the radius of a conic.

name: RandomPointIn
description: Creates a random point inside a given polygon or closed conic.

name: Ray
description: Creates a ray starting at a point through a point.

name: RigidPolygon
description:
Creates a copy of any polygon that can only be translated by dragging its first vertex and rotated by dragging its
second vertex.

name: Sector
description: Yields a conic sector between two points on the conic section and calculates its area.

name: Segment
description: This command differs among variants of English:

name: Semicircle
description: Creates a semicircle above the segment between the two points and displays its length in Algebra View .

name: Slope
description: Returns the slope of the given line.

name: Tangent
description: Creates (all) tangents through the point to the conic section.

name: TriangleCenter
description: This command differs among variants of English:

name: TriangleCurve
description:
Creates implicit polynomial, whose equation in barycentric coordinates with respect to
points P , Q , R is given by the fourth parameter; the barycentric coordinates are referred to as A , B , C .
syntax: TriangleCurve( <Point P>, <Point Q>, <Point R>, <Equation in A, B, C> )
TriangleCurve(P, Q, R, (A - B)*(B - C)*(C - A) = 0)
TriangleCurve(A, B, C, A² + B² + C² - 2B C - 2C A - 2A B = 0)
TriangleCurve(A, B, C, B C + C A + A B = 0)

name: Trilinear
description:
creates a point whose trilinear coordinates are the given numbers
with respect to triangle with given points.

name: Union
description: Joins the two lists and removes elements that appear multiple times.

name: Type
description:
For conics and quadrics this command returns a number representing the conic/quadric type according to the table below.
In this context, an empty conic (or quadric) is one whose coefficients are defined, but that does not contain any real
point, e.g. x 2 + y 2 = -1. For conics, GeoGebra distinguishes double line (special case of parallel lines with distance
0) and single line (special case of circle with infinite diameter, may result from circle inversion). For quadrics there
is no such distinction.

name: Vertex
description: Returns (all) vertices of the conic section.
syntax: Vertex((x + y < 3) && (x - y > 1)) returns point A = (2, 1) .
Vertex((y > x²) ∧ (y < x)) returns two points A = (0, 0) and B = (1, 1) .
